title: Benzenoids with the smallest Kemeny constant
statement: A benzenoid system with h hexagons is a connected set of h cells of the hexagonal tiling, joined through shared edges, that encloses no hole; its molecular graph has the hexagons' corners as vertices and their sides as edges. Kemeny's constant K(G) of a connected graph is the expected time for the simple random walk to reach a target vertex drawn from the stationary distribution (the same for every start), K = sum over the eigenvalues lambda != 1 of the transition matrix of 1/(1 - lambda) = (1/(2m)) sum over pairs {i,j} of d_i d_j R_ij (R: resistance distance; d: degrees; m: number of edges). For each h, which benzenoid with h hexagons minimises K? The headline cell is h = 19: circumcoronene gives K = 14813904881/113347080 = 130.695072...; find a benzenoid with 19 hexagons and a smaller Kemeny constant, or prove that circumcoronene is the minimiser.
submission: Text file: 19 lines 'q r', the axial coordinates of the hexagons (the neighbours of (q, r) are (q+-1, r), (q, r+-1), (q+1, r-1) and (q-1, r+1)).
score: Kemeny's constant of the molecular graph, an exact rational number (smaller is better)

best_known.source: Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 9 November 2026: circumcoronene (C54H18), the best of a beam search over benzenoids with 10 to 19 hexagons (tools/benzenoid_beam.py)

context: Kemeny's constant measures how fast a random walk mixes on a network, and through K = Kf*(G)/(2m) it equals the degree-Kirchhoff (multiplicative degree-Kirchhoff) index of chemical graph theory divided by twice the number of bonds. For hexagonal chains, the unbranched catacondensed benzenoids, the extremes are known: the linear chain maximises Kemeny's constant and the helicene chain minimises it (Y. Yang and W. Li, MATCH 2026). Over all benzenoids, including pericondensed ones, our exhaustive computation up to h = 10 shows that the minimisers are the most compact systems (the fewest carbon atoms, 2h + 1 + ceil(sqrt(12h - 3)), as for coronene at h = 7), but compactness alone does not decide: at h = 6 three systems with 22 atoms have different constants (42.391, 42.678 and 43.299). Whether the coronene series (coronene, circumcoronene, ...) always minimises K when h = 3k(k+1) + 1 is open.
references: J. G. Kemeny, J. L. Snell, Finite Markov Chains (Van Nostrand, 1960)
H. Chen, F. Zhang, Resistance distance and the normalized Laplacian spectrum, Discrete Applied Math. 155 (2007) 654-661 (degree-Kirchhoff index; K = Kf*/2m)

Y. Yang, W. Li, Extremal hexagonal chains with respect to the Kemeny's constant, MATCH Commun. Math. Comput. Chem. 96 (2026) 625-646 (linear chain maximal, helicene minimal among hexagonal chains; read as data)
F. Harary, H. Harborth, Extremal animals, J. Combin. Inform. System Sci. 1 (1976) 1-8 (fewest vertices of a polyhex)
OEIS A018190 (number of benzenoids with h hexagons; our enumeration reproduces 1, 1, 3, 7, 22, 81, 331, 1435, 6505, 30086)

novelty.verdict: new as stated. Kemeny's constant has been studied for hexagonal chains (unbranched catacondensed systems) and for special families; no work was found on its minimum over all benzenoid systems with h hexagons, and the values below are not in any table.
closest: Y. Yang and W. Li, Kemeny's constant of hexagonal chains (MATCH, 2026): extremes among unbranched catacondensed benzenoids. Here the class is all benzenoids, and the minimisers found are compact pericondensed systems, not chains.
Li, Chen and Liu (arXiv:2504.12781): Kemeny's constant of iterated hexagonal graphs, a family of formulas, not an extremal problem.

first_values.note: Exact for h <= 10: every benzenoid enumerated (counts agree with OEIS A018190) and the three smallest recomputed in exact rational arithmetic (tools/benzenoids.py). For h >= 11 the values are the best found by a beam search of width 60 (tools/benzenoid_beam.py), upper bounds only.

baseline.text: 14813904881/113347080 = 130.695072877... for h = 19 (circumcoronene, `refs/benzenoid-kemeny.txt`), held by Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 9 November 2026 as the best value found; the beam search over h = 10 to 19 found nothing smaller. No lower bound beyond the trivial one is proved.
